title: Can an ant survive falling from a plane?

lines.text: Chat asked me... if an ant fell out of an airplane... would it survive?
Let's find out. Ready, chat? Blocks up!
This is Antony. He's a toy ant. Real bugs, we just watch.
One stone block. One Antony. Three... two... one!
Safety first! His cousin Andy gets a parachute. Blocks up!
Soft landing. But wait... Antony landed soft too. No parachute!
When you're tiny, you're so light that the air pushes back almost as hard as gravity pulls.
That's called terminal velocity. The fastest you can fall.
An ant falls about as fast as you walk. A cat, as fast as a car. A person, even faster. So we keep our feet on the ground!
And from an airplane? The fall won't hurt an ant. But the cold up there? Brrr.
Giants? Gravity is the boss. Ants? The air is.

cards.meaning: The fastest something can fall: when the air pushes back as hard as gravity pulls.

cards.sub: J.B.S. Haldane, "On Being the Right Size" (1926)
